title: UNIT 6: SOLID FIGURES
notes:
✓ Solid figure → a three-dimensional object having length, width and height.

◆ Main solids → Prism, Cylinder, Pyramid, Cone, Sphere and Frustum.

✓ Surface area → the total area occupied by the surfaces of a solid.

✓ Volume → the amount of space occupied by a solid.

title: 6.1 PRISMS
notes:
✓ Prism → a solid with two congruent and parallel polygonal bases connected by lateral faces.

◆ Lateral faces → faces joining the two bases.

✓ Altitude (h) → perpendicular distance between the two bases.

◆ Right prism → altitude is perpendicular to the base.

For a right prism:
✓ LSA = p × h
✓ TSA = LSA + 2BA
✓ V = BA × h

p → perimeter of the base
BA → area of one base
h → altitude

title: TRIANGULAR PRISM EXAMPLE
notes:
Example: A right triangular prism has a triangular base with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm and height 6 cm.

✓ Base area = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²

✓ LSA = (3 + 4 + 5) × 6 = 72 cm²

✓ TSA = 72 + 2(6) = 84 cm²

✓ V = 6 × 6 = 36 cm³.

title: RECTANGULAR PRISM
notes:
For a rectangular prism with length l, width w and height h:

✓ BA = lw
✓ LSA = 2(l + w)h
✓ TSA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh
✓ V = lwh

Example: l = 3 cm, w = 2 cm, h = 4 cm.

✓ BA = 3 × 2 = 6 cm²
✓ V = 6 × 4 = 24 cm³
✓ TSA = 52 cm².

title: CYLINDER
notes:
✓ Cylinder → a solid having two congruent, parallel circular bases.

r → radius of base
h → altitude/height

✓ Base area = πr²
✓ Circumference = 2πr

✓ LSA = 2πrh
✓ TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r)
✓ V = πr²h

The curved surface area is the lateral surface area.

title: 6.2 PYRAMIDS
notes:
✓ Pyramid → a solid with a polygonal base and an apex (vertex) not on the base. Every point of the base is joined to the apex.

◆ Base → polygonal region at the bottom.
◆ Apex → common vertex of the lateral faces.
✓ Altitude → perpendicular distance from the apex to the plane of the base.
◆ Lateral faces → triangular faces connecting the base to the apex.

If the base has n sides, the pyramid has n lateral faces.

title: REGULAR AND RIGHT PYRAMIDS
notes:
◆ Right pyramid → the altitude meets the base at its center.

◆ Oblique pyramid → the altitude does not meet the base at its center.

◆ Regular pyramid → the base is a regular polygon and all lateral edges are equal.

✓ Slant height (l) → altitude of a lateral triangular face of a regular pyramid.

title: SURFACE AREA OF A REGULAR PYRAMID
notes:
For a regular pyramid:

✓ LSA = 1/2 × p × l

✓ TSA = BA + LSA

where:
p → perimeter of the base
l → slant height
BA → base area

Example: A regular square pyramid has base side 4 cm and slant height 5 cm.

✓ p = 4 × 4 = 16 cm
✓ LSA = 1/2 × 16 × 5 = 40 cm²
✓ BA = 4² = 16 cm²
✓ TSA = 40 + 16 = 56 cm².

title: VOLUME OF A PYRAMID
notes:
The volume of a pyramid is:

✓ V = 1/3 × BA × h

BA → area of the base
h → perpendicular height

Example: If BA = 30 cm² and h = 9 cm:

✓ V = 1/3 × 30 × 9 = 90 cm³.

title: CONE
notes:
✓ Cone → a solid with a circular base and one apex.

r → radius of circular base
h → perpendicular height
l → slant height

✓ Slant height:
l = √(h² + r²)

✓ Lateral surface area:
LSA = πrl

✓ Total surface area:
TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r)

✓ Volume:
V = 1/3πr²h.

title: CONE EXAMPLE
notes:
Example: A cone has radius 8 m and height 6 m.

✓ l = √(8² + 6²)
  = √100
  = 10 m

✓ LSA = π × 8 × 10 = 80π m²

✓ Volume = 1/3 × π × 8² × 6 = 128π m³.

title: HORIZONTAL CROSS-SECTIONS
notes:
✓ A horizontal cross-section is the intersection obtained when a pyramid or cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base.

✓ A horizontal cross-section of a triangular pyramid is a triangular region similar to its base.

✓ Corresponding lengths of similar cross-sections are proportional to their distances from the vertex.

If the cross-section is at distance k from the vertex and the pyramid height is h, the scale factor is k/h.

title: SPHERE
notes:
✓ Sphere → a three-dimensional solid whose surface consists of points at the same distance from its center.

r → radius

✓ Surface area:
SA = 4πr²

✓ Volume:
V = 4/3πr³

In terms of diameter d:
✓ SA = πd²
✓ V = πd³/6.

title: GREAT CIRCLE AND SMALL CIRCLE
notes:
When a plane cuts a sphere, the cross-section is a circle.

◆ Great circle → cross-section formed when the plane passes through the center of the sphere. Its radius equals the sphere's radius.

◆ Small circle → cross-section formed when the plane does not pass through the center.

✓ A great circle divides a sphere into two equal parts.

title: HEMISPHERE
notes:
✓ Hemisphere → one of the two equal parts of a sphere formed by a great circle.

For a hemisphere of radius r:

✓ Curved surface area = 2πr²
✓ Total surface area including circular base = 3πr²
✓ Volume = 2/3πr³.

title: 6.3 FRUSTUM OF A PYRAMID
notes:
✓ Frustum of a pyramid → the part of a pyramid between its base and a cross-section formed by cutting the pyramid with a plane parallel to its base.

◆ The two parallel faces are the bases.
◆ Other faces are lateral faces.
✓ For a regular pyramid frustum, lateral faces are congruent isosceles trapeziums.
✓ Altitude → perpendicular distance between the two bases.
✓ Slant height → altitude of a lateral face.

title: FRUSTUM OF A REGULAR PYRAMID
notes:
If p and p′ are the perimeters of the lower and upper bases and l is the slant height:

✓ LSA = 1/2 × l(p + p′)

✓ TSA = LSA + A + A′

where A and A′ are the areas of the lower and upper bases.

For a square frustum with side lengths s and s′:
✓ LSA = 2l(s + s′)
✓ TSA = 2l(s + s′) + s² + s′².

title: FRUSTUM OF A CONE
notes:
✓ A frustum of a cone is the part of a cone between its base and a cross-section formed by a plane parallel to the base.

r → radius of larger base
r′ → radius of smaller base
h → altitude
l → slant height

✓ Slant height:
l = √(h² + (r − r′)²)

✓ Lateral surface area:
LSA = πl(r + r′)

✓ Total surface area:
TSA = πl(r + r′) + πr² + πr′².

title: VOLUME OF A FRUSTUM
notes:
For a frustum of a pyramid or cone:

✓ V = 1/3 × h(A + A′ + √(AA′))

A and A′ → areas of the two bases
h → altitude of the frustum.

For a circular cone:
✓ V = 1/3πh(r² + r′² + rr′).

✓ This formula can also be obtained by subtracting the volume of the smaller cone from the larger cone.

title: FRUSTUM VOLUME EXAMPLE
notes:
Example: A frustum of a cone has radii 3 m and 5 m and height 12 m.

✓ V = 1/3π(12)(3² + 5² + 3×5)

= 4π(9 + 25 + 15)

= 196π m³.

✓ Always use the two base radii and perpendicular height in the frustum formula.

title: KEY FORMULAS — UNIT 6
notes:
◆ PRISM:
✓ LSA = ph
✓ TSA = ph + 2BA
✓ V = BAh

◆ CYLINDER:
✓ LSA = 2πrh
✓ TSA = 2πr(h + r)
✓ V = πr²h

◆ PYRAMID:
✓ LSA = 1/2pl
✓ TSA = BA + 1/2pl
✓ V = 1/3BAh

◆ CONE:
✓ LSA = πrl
✓ TSA = πr(l + r)
✓ V = 1/3πr²h
✓ l = √(h² + r²)

◆ SPHERE:
✓ SA = 4πr²
✓ V = 4/3πr³

◆ FRUSTUM:
✓ LSA of regular pyramid = 1/2l(p + p′)
✓ LSA of cone = πl(r + r′)
✓ V = 1/3h(A + A′ + √AA′)
✓ V(cone frustum) = 1/3πh(r² + r′² + rr′).

title: EXAM REMINDERS
notes:
✓ Distinguish radius from diameter: d = 2r.

✓ Use perpendicular height h for volume, not slant height.

✓ For a regular pyramid, LSA = 1/2pl.

✓ For a cone, calculate slant height using Pythagoras when needed.

✓ For a frustum, identify both base dimensions.

✓ For composed solids, separate the solid into familiar shapes.

✓ Add volumes of joined parts and subtract removed parts.

✓ For surface area, count only the surfaces that are actually exposed.

✓ Volume units → cm³, m³, etc.

✓ Surface-area units → cm², m², etc.
